findings.description: Long-lived AWS access key material is embedded in Terraform user_data and exported on the instance. It is exposed through source control, Terraform state/plans, and instance user-data retrieval, enabling anyone obtaining it to authenticate as the associated IAM principal.

No metadata_options configuration requires IMDSv2; the instance can use IMDSv1. An SSRF flaw on this internet-exposed host could retrieve any instance-profile credentials without the IMDSv2 token protection.
The EBS volume does not set encrypted = true, so its encryption relies on an account-level default not established by this configuration. Data on the volume may therefore be stored unencrypted.

This snapshot is created from a volume whose encryption is not enforced. EBS snapshots inherit source-volume encryption status, so this configuration can create a snapshot containing data at rest without encryption.
TCP port 22 is open to 0.0.0.0/0, exposing remote administration to the entire internet and enabling broad scanning and password/key attack attempts.
The security group permits all protocols and ports to 0.0.0.0/0. A compromised web host can use unrestricted egress for data exfiltration or command-and-control.
The bucket receiving VPC flow logs has no server-side encryption configuration. Flow-log objects may be stored without encryption at rest unless an external account default is relied on.

No S3 public-access-block controls are configured for the flow-log bucket. Future ACL or bucket-policy changes could make sensitive network telemetry public without this account- or bucket-level guardrail.
